 Meesho’s Vidit Aatrey buys Rs 83.8cr villa plots from Byju Raveendran’s family in B’luru 
 Trending Oil Price Today Stock Market Today Nvidia Rene Hass Gold Rates Today US Flight Disruptions Jensen Huang Oil Price Today Stock Market Today Nvidia Rene Hass Gold Rates Today US Flight Disruptions Jensen Huang Oil Price Today Stock Market Today Nvidia Rene Hass Gold Rates Today US Flight Disruptions Jensen Huang Meesho’s Vidit Aatrey buys Rs 83.8cr villa plots from Byju Raveendran’s family in B’luru 
 Shilpa Phadnis / Nov 16, 2026, 20:06 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Bengaluru: Meesho co-founder and CEO Vidit Aatrey has purchased two adjoining luxury residential villa plots in Bengaluru from members of Byju Raveendran’s family for a combined Rs 83.8 crore, according to property registration data sourced from proptech platform Zapkey. The transactions, executed through two separate sale deeds on July 24, 2026, and registered on July 27, involve a combined land parcel of 33,485 sq ft at Epsilon Residential Villas in Bengaluru East. In the first transaction, Aatrey purchased an 18,305 sq ft plot from Divya Gokulnath, wife of Byju Raveendran, for Rs 48.11 crore. The deal values the land at approximately Rs 26,280 per sq ft. In the second transaction, he acquired an adjoining 15,180 sq ft parcel from Deeptha Akhila Raghavan, wife of Riju Raveendran, Byju Raveendran’s brother, for Rs 35.70 crore. This translates to around Rs 23,521 per sq ft. The blended acquisition cost works out to approximately Rs 25,029 per sq ft. An email sent to Meesho didn’t elicit a response till press time. The transactions come amid ongoing insolvency and legal proceedings involving Think & Learn, the parent company of edtech firm BYJU’S. The sale deeds, drafted by law firm Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, contain extensive indemnification clauses and representations from the sellers. Join conversation

 Both sellers have warranted that the properties are self-acquired, free of encumbrances and not subject to attachments or proceedings under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code , the Prevention of Money Laundering Act or tax laws. The sellers have also provided assurances on the properties’ ownership and legal status, seeking to protect the buyer against potential claims arising from the ongoing proceedings surrounding the edtech company.
